signals.entity: Central Bank of the Republic of Kosovo (BQK/CBK)
signals.signal: NEW EDITION, SUPERSEDES THE BASELINE. CBK published 'Përdorimi i kartelave në Kosovë' dated GUSHT (August) 2026, with data at 31/12/2025. ATM fleet: 686 terminals (2023: 583; 2024: 635), annual growth 8.03% after 8.92% and 9.18%. Table 1 splits the 686 by function: ALL 686 offer cash withdrawal, 394 offer CASH DEPOSIT, and only 57 offer CREDIT TRANSFER. Against the prior edition (377 deposit-capable and 53 credit-transfer-capable of 635 at 31/12/2024) that is +17 deposit-capable machines on +51 total machines. THE MATERIAL CORRECTION: the deposit-capable SHARE therefore FELL from 59.4% to 57.4% during 2025 - the previous run's reading that 'deposit-capable units are the visible growth vector (+51 in one year)' was wrong; deposit capability grew only a third as fast as the fleet, so the cash-in gap WIDENED to 292 machines (42.6%) that cannot take a deposit and 629 (91.7%) that cannot originate a credit transfer. ATMs are heavily concentrated: Prishtinë 31.49%, Prizren 7.29%, Ferizaj 6.85%, Gjilan 5.83%, Pejë 4.96%, Gjakovë 4.52%, Mitrovicë 4.08%.
signals.source_name: CBK - 'Përdorimi i kartelave në Kosovë', August 2026 edition (data to 31/12/2025), Payment Systems Department
signals.implies: The single hardest quantified number in this market: 292 Kosovo ATMs cannot accept a cash deposit and 629 cannot originate a transfer, in a euroised cash economy. And the gap is getting WIDER, not narrower - banks are adding dispensers faster than recyclers. That is the core Printec cash-recycler / cash-in-ATM case, plus ATM application software to add transfer and bill-payment functions to the 91.7% of machines that lack it. Use the widening-gap framing, not the old closing-gap framing, in any bank conversation.
signals.likelihood: Structural market gap confirmed over three consecutive annual editions; conversion is steady rather than tender-driven
signals.followup: ARCHIVE THIS PDF LOCALLY. Ask CBK Payment Systems (payment.systems@bqk-kos.org, +383 38 222 055) for the PER-BANK breakdown of the 686/394/57 split, which the public report withholds - that single table would convert this market-level gap into a named target list. Note the URL is a dated wp-content path (2026/08), unlike the previous non-versioned repository path, so it should survive the next edition.

signals.entity: Central Bank of the Republic of Kosovo (BQK/CBK)
signals.signal: POS ACCEPTANCE EXPLODED IN 2025. Same August-2026 CBK report, Table 2 and Figure 3: POS terminals in Kosovo reached 30,295 at 31/12/2025, from 20,913 at 31/12/2024 and 17,187 at 31/12/2023 - annual growth of 44.86% in 2025 after 21.68% in 2024, i.e. +9,382 terminals in a single year. All 30,295 are EFTPOS. The number offering a cash-withdrawal (cashback) function jumped to 245, from just 18 a year earlier. POS is even more concentrated than ATM: Prishtinë 42.01%, Ferizaj 11.00%, Prizren 7.77%. Card base: 1,863,188 customer cards at 31/12/2025, +10.64% YoY (2024: 1,684,034), of which 89,340 are e-money cards issued by non-bank financial institutions; debit +10.39%, credit +12.11%. Per-million-inhabitant density on a 1.58m population: 434.2 ATMs and 19,174 POS.
signals.source_name: CBK - 'Përdorimi i kartelave në Kosovë', August 2026 edition (data to 31/12/2025)
signals.implies: A 45% one-year expansion of the acceptance estate is the largest single movement in Kosovo's payment infrastructure and was invisible to the previous run. Nearly ten thousand terminals were deployed in twelve months - that is terminal supply, estate management, key injection and PCI/HSM work at scale, and it is happening now rather than in prospect. The 18-to-245 jump in cashback-enabled POS is a second, distinct opening: merchant-based cash-out is starting to substitute for ATMs in Kosovo, which both threatens the dispenser-only estate and creates a POS-based cash-access product to sell.
signals.likelihood: High that expansion continues into 2026 - the growth rate has accelerated for two consecutive years and the pending Payment Services law adds a universal-acceptance direction of travel
signals.followup: Identify WHO deployed the +9,382 terminals in 2025 - which acquirers and which terminal vendors - because that tells you whether Printec's acceptance position in Kosovo is growing or being taken. Ask CBK for the acquirer-level split. Then investigate the cashback jump (18 to 245): which bank is driving merchant cash-out and on what hardware.

signals.entity: Central Bank of the Republic of Kosovo (BQK/CBK)
signals.signal: Transaction-mix evidence from the same August-2026 CBK report (Figure 28, data for 2025). By NUMBER of card transactions: POS payments 69.4%, ATM withdrawals 26.4%, ATM deposits and credit transfers and POS cash-out making up the remaining ~4.2%. By VALUE the picture inverts: ATM withdrawals 50.2%, ATM DEPOSITS 32.1%, POS payments only 17.8%. The report's own conclusion is that citizens use cards mainly for small-value payments. ATM withdrawal transaction NUMBERS grew about 6.65% during 2025. Separately (section 4.3): digital wallets were offered by three commercial banks and four non-bank financial institutions during 2025, carrying 736,614 payments worth EUR 23,157,130; CBK attributes the visible jump to APPLE PAY LAUNCHING IN KOSOVO IN AUGUST 2025.
signals.source_name: CBK - 'Përdorimi i kartelave në Kosovë', August 2026 edition (data to 31/12/2025)
signals.implies: ATM deposits already carry 32.1% of all card-transaction VALUE on only 394 deposit-capable machines - the highest-value work in the country is being done by the smallest and least-equipped part of the estate. That is the quantified ROI argument for recyclers: each deposit-capable unit is carrying disproportionate value, so adding cash-in capability to the 292 dispenser-only machines has a measurable, defensible business case rather than a speculative one. Meanwhile ATM withdrawal volume is still GROWING 6.65% a year, so this is not a declining-cash market where self-service investment is hard to justify.
signals.followup: Build the recycler business case for a named Kosovo bank off the 32.1%-of-value-on-394-machines figure. Ask CBK whether the deposit value figure includes third-party/business deposits, which is what BKT's unique-code service and ProCredit's over-EUR-10,000 deposit service are aimed at.

signals.entity: Central Bank of the Republic of Kosovo (BQK/CBK)
signals.signal: On 15/07/2026 CBK announced it had begun EU-supported activities to establish the KOSOVO COUNTERFEIT MONITORING SYSTEM ('Sistemi i Kosovës për Monitorimin e Falsifikimit të Parasë'). CBK also published the 2025 Financial Stability Report on 04/08/2026 ('Kosovo's financial system maintains high stability and resilience to risks'), submitted its 2025 Annual Report to the Assembly on 30/06/2026 after board approval on 29/06/2026, and on 03/07/2026 Governor Ismaili spoke on governing innovation and ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE responsibly in the interest of financial stability. SOURCING NOTE: these are the headlines and publication dates as they appeared on CBK's own homepage; the individual news pages could not be opened (see access issues) so the bodies of the 15/07/2026 and 04/08/2026 items are NOT verified beyond their titles and dates.
signals.source_name: CBK homepage news listing (bqk-kos.org), archived copy of 21/08/2026
signals.implies: A national counterfeit monitoring system is the ECB-model Counterfeit Monitoring System framework. Standing it up obliges banks to run banknote authentication and fitness testing to a tested-and-certified standard and to report suspected counterfeits centrally - which lands directly on note validators inside ATMs and recyclers, on back-office banknote processing machines, and on the certification status of every cash-accepting machine in the country. Combined with the 292 non-deposit ATMs, this is a compliance-driven reason to touch the whole estate rather than a discretionary upgrade. EU funding means the money is already committed.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High that this creates equipment-certification obligations on banks within 12-24 months; the implementation timetable is not published
signals.followup: PRIORITY: obtain the 15/07/2026 CBK press release in full and identify the EU instrument funding it and the implementation timetable. Ask the CBK Money and Banking Relations Department (Departamenti i Parave dhe Marrëdhënieve Bankare) what equipment testing/certification regime banks will have to meet and whether machine types will need to appear on a tested list, as in the ECB regime. That list is the gate every cash-handling vendor must pass.

signals.entity: Central Bank of the Republic of Kosovo (BQK/CBK)
signals.signal: [STANDING - approved 27/12/2023, in force 01/02/2024, re-verified this run because the previous run never captured it] The CBK Board approved the Regulation on Cash Operations, binding on CBK, banks, branches of foreign banks and other licensed financial institutions. Its published scope includes: procedures for handling and withdrawing from circulation euro banknotes and coins suspected of being counterfeit; criteria for exchanging damaged euro banknotes and coins; MINIMUM STANDARDS FOR FITNESS CHECKING AND RE-CIRCULATION OF EURO BANKNOTES AND COINS; standards for packaging euro banknotes and coins for deposit at CBK; conditions for cash payment transactions; rules on import/export of euro cash; and - the item that matters most here - 'PROCEDURES AND OBLIGATIONS FOR PROVIDERS OF CASH DEPOSIT OR WITHDRAWAL SERVICES THROUGH CUSTOMER-OPERATED MACHINES'. CBK subsequently published a 'Frequently Asked Questions on the Regulation on Cash Operations' document and, separately, a Plan for facilitated implementation committing within three months to a free phone line (0800-222-55), a complaints e-mail and a dedicated Viber number, easier account-opening in Serb-majority municipalities including the four northern ones, and temporary suspension of the CBK branch/office-opening fee to encourage licensed non-bank financial institutions (especially bureaux de change) to open offices there.
signals.source_name: CBK - 'The CBK Board approved the Regulation on Cash Operations' and 'The CBK publishes Frequently Asked Questions on the Regulation on Cash Operations' (archived copies of the CBK news pages)
signals.implies: Kosovo already has, in force, a national fitness-checking and re-circulation standard for euro cash AND an explicit regulatory category for 'customer-operated machines' that take deposits or dispense cash. That is the legal hook underneath every recycler sale in this market: a recycler must authenticate and fitness-sort to standard, and its operator carries named obligations. It also legitimises non-bank cash-machine operators. Pair it with the new Counterfeit Monitoring System (15/07/2026) - the regulation set the standard, the CMS builds the reporting machinery around it.
signals.followup: Obtain the regulation's full text and the FAQ from CBK and extract the exact fitness-checking and re-circulation requirements and the obligations placed on operators of customer-operated machines - specifically whether machine types must be tested/listed. This is the compliance spine for every recycler proposal in Kosovo and it was entirely absent from the previous run's file.

signals.entity: TEB Sh.A. (TEB Kosova, BNP Paribas / TEB group)
signals.signal: First-party locator counts taken from the bank's own site on 27/08/2026: the TEB ATM page lists 87 ATM locations and the TEB branches page lists 35 branches - roughly 2.5 machines per branch. Named ATM sites include two separate machines at Prishtina Mall (one inside the building, one outside in the main car park), Royal Mall, the Shell filling station at Veternik, the corporate branch at km 7 of the Prishtinë-Ferizaj highway, and Taslixhe. Neither page states how many machines accept deposits, and neither uses the words deposit/deponim or 24/7. SEPARATELY, TEB markets a service headlined 'Tërheq cash pa kartelë në ATM të bankës TEB përmes QR Code' - CARDLESS CASH WITHDRAWAL AT TEB ATMs VIA QR CODE - described on the bank's own campaign page as 'the newest ATM service for our customers': customers withdraw from a TEB ATM without needing their debit card. The campaign page carries no publication date.
signals.source_name: TEB Sh.A. - TEB ATM locator, TEB Degët (branches) page, and the campaign page 'Tërheq cash pa kartelë në ATM të bankës TEB përmes QR Code'
signals.implies: TEB's 87 machines are the second-largest named self-service estate disclosed in Kosovo after Raiffeisen's 168, and this is the first time it has been counted. The QR cardless-withdrawal launch is more strategically interesting than it looks: cardless flows require new ATM application software and a mobile-to-ATM token exchange, which means TEB has recently touched its ATM software layer - the moment when a bank is most open to a wider self-service conversation, and evidence that its estate can carry modern applications. The complete absence of deposit or 24/7 language on the TEB estate pages, against a national picture where 42.6% of ATMs cannot take a deposit, makes TEB a prime suspect for a dispenser-heavy fleet.
signals.likelihood: High that the QR service is live (it is marketed as current on the bank's own site); Medium on the fleet count, which is a locator snapshot rather than a disclosed figure
signals.followup: Ask TEB how many of the 87 machines are deposit-capable or recycling, who supplied the cardless-QR ATM application, and whether the QR rollout covered the whole fleet or a subset. TEB is a BNP Paribas/TEB (Türk Ekonomi Bankası) joint-venture subsidiary, so check whether ATM software and hardware decisions are taken in Istanbul rather than Prishtina. TEB's WordPress REST API is authentication-locked (401), so counts must be re-derived from the HTML each run.

signals.signal: BKT Kosova offers business customers CASH DEPOSIT AT ITS ATMs USING A UNIQUE CODE INSTEAD OF A CARD. The bank's own product page states the transaction is executed via a Unique Code generated by the Business E-Banking system and sent to the authorised business user; the code identifies the transaction precisely and links it to the correct business account, ELIMINATING THE NEED FOR A PHYSICAL CARD. BKT positions it explicitly for businesses that DELEGATE cash depositing to authorised employees, reducing day-to-day operational complexity. Activation requires a visit to the nearest branch to complete the configuration. Page published 06/10/2025 and last modified 06/10/2025 per the page's own structured-data timestamps. The same service appears in the site's business menu as 'Shërbime në ATM - Deponim me kod unik'.
signals.source_name: BKT Kosova - 'Deponim me kod unik në ATM' (bank's own product page; dates from the page's schema.org datePublished/dateModified)
signals.implies: Proof that BKT Kosova already runs DEPOSIT-CAPABLE ATMs and has built a cardless, code-based business cash-in flow on top of them - i.e. it is competing for merchant cash handling at the machine rather than the counter. This is exactly the SME cash-in use case that justifies recyclers, and it is a working competitive benchmark to show other Kosovo banks. It also means BKT's ATM application layer supports token-based transactions, so an estate refresh conversation there is about capacity and recycling, not basic capability. Together with TEB's QR cardless withdrawal, two of Kosovo's larger banks have now moved to cardless self-service flows within a year.
signals.likelihood: Live service, published by the bank
signals.followup: Ask BKT Kosova how many of its ATMs accept the unique-code deposit, whether the machines are recyclers or cash-in-only, and who supplied the ATM application. Then use this as the reference case when pitching business cash-in to BPB, Banka Ekonomike and NLB Kosovo, which do not appear to offer an equivalent.

signals.signal: Q2/H1-2026 published financial statements (PDF dated to the bank's July-2026 content folder, figures at 30/06/2026 against 31/03/2026): total assets EUR 1,639.3m from EUR 1,552.4m in the previous quarter, +5.6% in one quarter; loans and advances to customers EUR 1,039.6m from EUR 978.5m; customer deposits EUR 1,259.1m from EUR 1,217.1m; total shareholders' equity EUR 211.5m from EUR 200.6m; current-year profit EUR 18.36m at 30/06/2026 against EUR 9.08m at 31/03/2026. Property and equipment EUR 22.96m from EUR 22.59m - marginally up, unusual among peers.
signals.source_name: BKT Kosova - Pasqyrat Financiare Q2 2026 (published financial statements)
signals.implies: BKT Kosova is growing its balance sheet faster than any other Kosovo bank in this set (+5.6% assets in a single quarter) and is one of only two here with RISING property and equipment - it is investing in physical infrastructure while peers hold flat. Combined with the cardless business-deposit service, BKT is the Kosovo bank most visibly spending on the cash and channel layer, and therefore the best-qualified target for a recycler and estate proposal.
signals.followup: Get BKT Kosova's 2025 annual report for the branch and ATM counts, which the quarterly statements do not carry, and establish what the rising property-and-equipment line is being spent on. Note BKT Kosova's branch/ATM locator loads its data by AJAX, so the fleet could not be counted from the HTML this run.

signals.source_name: NLB Banka sh.a., Prishtinë - 'About the Bank' key data page (sourced by the bank to its Annual Report 2025)
signals.implies: Confirms rather than advances the position: a 100+ machine fleet in Kosovo under NLB Group's publicly committed 'ATM & CDS network upgrade at Group level driving cash out of branches' programme from the 07/05/2026 Investor Day. coverage_notes: Fresh full run (no checkpoint existed). Covered: BKT Kosova, TEB Kosova, ProCredit Bank Kosova, BPB (Banka per Biznes), NLB Banka Kosovo, Banka Ekonomike, plus the Central Bank of Kosovo as the regulator behind all six. Entry points deliberately varied from the previous run: bank WordPress REST APIs (bpbbank.com wp-json surfaced a news item one day old and dated the tender board), locator-page HTML parsing with the pages' own data-type attributes (ProCredit's markup exposes an 'ATM Zone' category invisible in the rendered page), tender-board PDFs opened individually, quarterly published financial statements extracted locally with pdfminer, and the Internet Archive CDX index used to enumerate CBK URLs that the live site will not serve. BIGGEST WIN: the August-2026 edition of CBK's 'Perdorimi i kartelave ne Kosove' (data to 31/12/2025) was found and fully extracted - it is three weeks old, supersedes the baseline's September-2025 edition, and materially CORRECTS it: the deposit-capable share of Kosovo's ATM fleet FELL during 2025 (377/635 = 59.4% to 394/686 = 57.4%), so the cash-in gap widened rather than narrowed. It also reveals a 44.86% one-year explosion in POS terminals to 30,295 that the previous run never saw. SECOND: the baseline's unresolved Isbank/Banka Ekonomike cutover date is now RESOLVED to 01/09/2025 - the same customer notice appears twice in the news archive, originally dated 28.08.2025 and re-posted 23.04.2026. Do not brief it as a live integration. THIRD: two Kosovo banks have gone cardless at the ATM within a year - BKT's unique-code business cash deposit (06/10/2025) and TEB's QR cardless withdrawal - and first-party locator counts were established for TEB (87 ATMs, 35 branches) and ProCredit (29 points: 15 branch+ATM, 13 stand-alone ATM, 1 ATM Zone), neither of which existed in the baseline. GENUINE GAPS: (a) NLB Group's H1-2026 interim report could not be retrieved, so no Kosovo fleet figure has been reconciled against group disclosure - the same debt the previous run flagged, still outstanding; (b) BKT Kosova's branch/ATM locator loads by AJAX and could not be counted; (c) BPB's ATM locator likewise exposes no machine-readable data, so BPB's fleet size remains unknown; (d) the bodies of two CBK news items (15/07/2026 counterfeit monitoring system, 04/08/2026 Financial Stability Report 2025) are unverified beyond title and date, and an untitled CBK press release of 19/08/2026 could not be identified at all; (e) the TIPS Clone November-2026 onboarding window for CBK and the Assembly's re-passage of the Draft Law on Payment Services could not be re-checked this run because WebSearch was unavailable and CBK's news pages are blocked - both remain as the previous run left them and should be re-verified next run.
access_issues:
1) WEBSEARCH UNAVAILABLE FOR THE ENTIRE RUN. The session's web-search budget (200/200 calls) was already exhausted by earlier agents before this task started, so NOT A SINGLE search query could be issued. All 16 signals were obtained by direct fetch of known/derived URLs, by parsing site markup and REST APIs, and via the Internet Archive CDX index. This mainly cost discovery of PRESS coverage and of pages whose URLs could not be guessed; primary-source coverage is unaffected and is arguably better than a search-led run. Raising CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION would materially improve the next run.
2) bqk-kos.org SITS BEHIND A CLOUDFLARE JS INTERSTITIAL for all HTML paths. Every route was tried and logged: plain curl HEAD -> HTTP 403; desktop Chrome User-Agent plus full browser header set (Accept, Accept-Language, Referer, sec-ch-ua, sec-fetch-*, Upgrade-Insecure-Requests) -> still 403 with a 'Just a moment...' challenge body; WebFetch -> HTTP 403; /wp-json/ and /wp-json/wp/v2/posts -> 403; /feed/ -> HTTP 200 but an empty 501-byte RSS document. BLOCKED URLS INCLUDE https://bqk-kos.org/?lang=en, https://bqk-kos.org/sistemi-i-pagesave/?lang=en, https://bqk-kos.org/wp-json/wp/v2/posts and https://bqk-kos.org/news/bqk-nis-aktivitetet-e-mbeshtetura-nga-bashkimi-evropian-per-themelimin-e-sistemit-te-kosoves-per-monitorimin-e-falsifikimit-te-parase/.
   TWO WORKING ROUTES WERE FOUND AND ARE WORTH REUSING NEXT RUN. (a) STATIC ASSET PATHS ARE NOT CHALLENGED: https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/... and https://bqk-kos.org/repository/docs/... return 200 to plain curl. That is how the August-2026 card report PDF (640KB) and the monthly payment-system XLSX feed (100KB) were retrieved. Go straight to the asset path and skip the HTML. (b) THE INTERNET ARCHIVE CDX API enumerates bqk-kos.org URLs and serves archived copies of the HTML pages, including a 21/08/2026 homepage snapshot that yielded the dated news listing. NOTE the archive is partial - individual /news/ pages returned 404 at the archive, which is why two 2026 news bodies remain unverified. The documented advice that a desktop User-Agent defeats bqk-kos.org 403s is NO LONGER TRUE; the site has moved to a full JS challenge. Escalation to Claude-in-Chrome was NOT performed - the static-asset and archive routes delivered the highest-value document (the card report) without it.
3) teb-kos.com WordPress REST API returns 401 rest_not_logged_in for /wp-json/wp/v2/types and all post types, so TEB counts had to be derived by parsing location-info blocks out of the page HTML; they will need re-deriving each run.
4) BPB's tender-board 'Shkarko' buttons all point to https://bpbbank.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/dummy.pdf - a placeholder, not a document. No tender text could be read; the lot titles and their 09/07/2025 post dates came from the WordPress REST API instead. Logged rather than dropped.
5) BKT Kosova's and BPB's branch/ATM locators render their points by AJAX with no data attributes or JSON payload in the served HTML, so neither fleet could be counted. ProCredit's and TEB's locators DO ship their data in the HTML and were counted.
6) NLB Group investor-relations index (https://www.nlb.si/investor-relations-reports) returned HTTP 404, so the H1-2026 interim report was not reached and the group-level reconciliation was not attempted.
7) pdftotext is not installed on this machine; all PDFs were extracted locally with pdfminer, which worked on every file including the 31-page CBK report.
operator_requests:
Nothing is paywalled, but four items need a human or a browser session:
1) CBK NEWS PAGES (Cloudflare JS challenge - needs a real browser). Please open and capture in full: (a) https://bqk-kos.org/news/bqk-nis-aktivitetet-e-mbeshtetura-nga-bashkimi-evropian-per-themelimin-e-sistemit-te-kosoves-per-monitorimin-e-falsifikimit-te-parase/ (15/07/2026, Kosovo Counterfeit Monitoring System - the single highest-value unverified item, because it likely carries equipment-certification obligations for every cash-accepting machine in Kosovo); (b) the 04/08/2026 Financial Stability Report 2025 announcement and the report PDF itself; (c) the untitled press release of 19/08/2026, which could not even be identified.
2) CBK PAYMENT SYSTEMS DEPARTMENT - a direct request, not a web fetch. Ask payment.systems@bqk-kos.org (+383 38 222 055) for the PER-BANK breakdown behind the 686 ATMs / 394 deposit-capable / 57 credit-transfer split, and for the acquirer-level split behind the +9,382 POS terminals added in 2025. Both are withheld from the public report and both would convert market-level gaps into named targets.
3) BPB PROCUREMENT - ask informata@bpbbank.com or +383 38 620 620 for the current holder and expiry of the bundled 'security services (cash-in-transit, guarding, monitoring centre) and ATM management' contract, and for inclusion on the invitation list. BPB states these invitations are also published in the daily newspapers, so a live notice may never appear online - worth someone monitoring Kosovo dailies.
4) PROCREDIT BANK KOSOVA - register as a supplier at kos.Procurement@procredit-group.com and ask whether tender T-0007-07-2026 (UPS and UPS batteries, closed 25/08/2026) was awarded or will be re-run. Low effort, open door.
Also worth flagging to the Orchestrator: NLB GROUP remains uncovered for a second consecutive run, and the Kosovo 'over 100 ATMs' figure still has no group-level cross-check.
